en: To reduce slightly; to cut; especially, to remove excess.
To decorate or adorn; especially of a Christmas tree.
Decoration; especially, decoration placed along edges or borders.
A haircut, especially a moderate one to touch up an existing style.
Physically fit.
Slender, lean.
In good order; properly managed or maintained.
With sails well trimmed.

trim.ety: From Middle English trimen, trymen, trümen, from Old English trymman (“to make firm; strengthen”), from Proto-West Germanic *trummjan, from Proto-Germanic *trumjaną (“to make fast; strengthen”), from Proto-Germanic *trumaz (“firm; strong; sound”).

ex.en: Trim the fat off the meat.
ex.ja: 肉から脂身を取りなさい。

ex.en: Do you want a trim?
ex.ja: 毛先をそろえますか。

ex.en: I thought I told you to trim your beard.
ex.ja: ひげを整えるようにあなたに言ったはずですが。

note.ja: 古英語 trymian（整える）から。「きちんと整える」→「刈り込む・切り詰める」。

en: A cloth-covered frame used for protection against rain or sun.
Anything that provides similar protection.
To cover or protect, as if by an umbrella.
To form the dome shape of an open umbrella.

umbrella.ety: Borrowed from Italian ombrella (“parasol, sunshade”), from Late Latin umbrella (influenced by umbra (“shadow, shade”)), from Latin umbella, from umbra + -la (diminutive suffix).

ex.en: I took my umbrella for fear of rain.
ex.ja: 雨が降るといけないので私はかさを持っていった。

ex.en: You had better take an umbrella with you.
ex.ja: 傘を持っていった方がいいよ。

ex.en: I'm pretty sure that this is his umbrella.
ex.ja: これは彼のかさだろう。

note.ja: イタリア語 ombrella（小さな日陰）から。ラテン語 umbra（陰）+ 縮小。もとは日傘。

en: A long journey, especially by ship.
To go on a long journey.

voyage.ety: From Middle English viage, borrowed from Anglo-Norman viage and Old French voiage, from Latin viaticum. The modern spelling is under the influence of Modern French voyage. Doublet of viaticum.

ex.en: Mary went on a voyage around the world.
ex.ja: メアリーは世界一周の航路に出た。

ex.en: The long voyage was a trial for us.
ex.ja: 長い船旅は私たちにとって試練であった。

ex.en: My health is not equal to the voyage.
ex.ja: 私の健康では航海に耐えられない。

note.ja: ラテン語 viaticum（旅の糧）から。via（道）。「長旅・航海」。convey、via と同じ。

en: The office or dominion of an abbot or abbess.
A monastery or society of people, secluded from the world and devoted to religion and celibacy, which is headed by an abbot or abbess; al…

abbey.ety: From A.D. 1250 in Middle English abbey, abbeye (“convent headed by an abbot”) (compare archaic English abbaye), itself borrowed from Old French abaïe, abbaïe, abeïe, abbeïe (Modern French abbaye) from Late Latin or Ecclesiastical Latin abbātia, from Classical Latin abbās (“abbot”). Doublet of abbacy and Opatija. See abbot.

note.ja: アラム語 abba（父）から。修道院長（abbot ＝ 父）が治める所 →「修道院」。

The result of adjusting something; a small change; a minor correction; a modification or alteration.

ex.ja: 最後の調整を完了するために五分ください。

ex.en: The decline isn't so sharp after seasonal adjustment.
ex.ja: 落ち込みは季節調整すればそれほど大きくない。

ex.en: You can adjust the seat height by moving the adjustment lever up.
ex.ja: 調節レバーを上に上げると座面の高さを調節できます。

note.ja: ad（〜に）+ just（ちょうど・正しい）+ ment。ちょうど合わせること →「調整・適応」。

en: The act or process of (physically or figuratively) attaching.
A strong bonding with or fondness for someone or something.

attachment.ety: From French attachement. By surface analysis, attach + -ment.

ex.en: I feel a strong attachment to this house.
ex.ja: この家に愛着を感じている。

ex.en: He has a great attachment to this town.
ex.ja: 彼はこの町に強い愛着を持っている。

ex.en: She had a great attachment to that old house.
ex.ja: 彼女はその古い家に強い愛着を持っていた。

en: The male ruler of a barony.
A male member of the lowest rank of English nobility (the equivalent rank in Scotland is lord).

baron.ety:
From Middle English baroun, from Old French baron, from Latin barōnem, from Proto-West Germanic *barō, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰer- (“to bear”). Cognate with Old High German *baro (“human being, man, freeman”), Old English bora (“a man who bears responsibility, one who is in charge, a ruler”), and perhaps to Old English beorn (“man, warrior”). Used in early Germanic law in the sense of "man, human being".
A Celtic origin has also been suggested; see the quote under sense 3 of Latin barō. However, the OED takes the hypothetical Proto-Celtic *bar- (“hero”) to be a figment.

note.ja: ゲルマン系の語で「男・戦士」から。→「男爵」→「大物（実業界の大立者）」。

en: A military aircraft designed to carry and drop bombs.
A person who sets bombs, especially as an act of terrorism.

en: A rabbit, especially a juvenile one.
A bunny girl: a nightclub waitress who wears a costume having rabbit ears and tail.
Easy or unchallenging.

Probably from Scottish Gaelic bun (“bottom, butt, stump, stub”), from Old Irish bun (“the thick end of anything, base, butt, foot”), from Proto-Celtic *bonus, though its origin is uncertain. Compare also English bum. Together with rabbit, bunny has largely displaced its former rhyme cony (see cony for more).

ex.en: The bunny jumped over the dog.
ex.ja: うさぎが、犬を飛び越えました。

en: A light source consisting of a wick embedded in a solid, flammable substance such as wax, tallow, or paraffin.
The protruding, removable portion of a filter, particularly a water filter.
To observe the growth of an embryo inside (an egg), using a bright light source.
To dry (greenware) prior to the firing cycle, setting the kiln at 200° Celsius until all water is removed from the greenware.

ex.en: A birthday cake with twelve candles on top.
ex.ja: ろうそくが１２本立った誕生日のケーキ。

ex.en: He was burning the candle at both ends.
ex.ja: 朝から晩まで忙しく働いていた。

ex.en: Please put some candles on the birthday cake.
ex.ja: バースデーケーキにろうそくを立ててください。

note.ja: ラテン語 candela（ろうそく）から。candere（白く輝く）。candid（率直な：白い）、candidate（白衣の候補者）も同じ。

en: Of an object, made by carving.

ex.en: The boy carved his name on the tree.
ex.ja: 少年は木に自分の名前を刻んだ。

ex.en: The boy carved his name in the tree.
ex.ja: 少年は木に自分の名前を刻んだ。

ex.en: Tony carved his name on a tree with a knife.
ex.ja: トニーはナイフで自分の名を木に刻んだ。

en: A group of people who sing together; a company of people who are trained to sing together.
One quarter of a cruciform church, or the architectural area of a church, generally used by the choir; often near the apse.
To sing in concert.

choir.ety: From Middle English quer, quere, from Old French quer, from Latin chorus, from Ancient Greek χορός (khorós, “company of dancers or singers”). Modern spelling influenced by chorus and French chœur. Doublet of quire, chorus, and hora. Displaced native Old English hād.

ex.en: How was choir practice?
ex.ja: 合唱の練習はどうだった？

ex.en: She has been invited to sing in a choir in a foreign country.
ex.ja: 彼女は海外の合唱団で歌わないかと誘われています。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 khoros（合唱隊）から。chorus と同じ語源。

zh: 離合器踏板 /离合器踏板

en: To seize, as though with claws.
To grip or grasp tightly.
The claw of a predatory animal or bird.
A grip, especially one seen as rapacious or evil.
Performing or tending to perform well in difficult, high-pressure situations.

clutch.ety:
From Middle English clucchen, clicchen, cluchen, clechen, cleken, from Old English clyċċan (“to clutch, clench”), from Proto-West Germanic *klukkjan, from Proto-Germanic *klukjaną, from Proto-Germanic *klu- (“to ball up, conglomerate, amass”), from Proto-Indo-European *glew- (“to ball up; lump, mass”).
Cognate with Swedish klyka (“clamp, fork, branch”). The noun is from Middle English cleche, cloche, cloke ("claw, talon, hand"; compare Scots cleuk, cluke, cluik (“claw, talon”)), of uncertain origin, with the form probably assimilated to the verb.
Alternative etymology derives Old English clyċċ

ex.en: He was caught in the clutches of the law.
ex.ja: 彼は法律の網にかかった。

ex.en: She clutched her baby in her arms.
ex.ja: 彼女は赤ん坊をしっかりと腕に抱きしめた。

ex.en: He clutched his wallet in his hand.
ex.ja: その子は手に財布をしっかり掴んでいた。

note.ja: 古英語 clyccan（握りしめる）から。「ぐっとつかむ」→ 動力をつかんで伝える装置 →「クラッチ」。

en: A fruit of the coconut palm (not a true nut), Cocos nucifera, having a fibrous husk surrounding a large seed.
A hard-shelled seed of this fruit, having white flesh and a fluid-filled central cavity.

coconut.ety: From coco + nut. In reference to assimilated Hispanic or black people, derived from the fruit's exotic origins. The slur originates from the idea that one is "brown on the outside, white on the inside". In reference to Polynesians, from the ubiquity of coconut palms in the area.

ex.en: I want to drink coconut milk.
ex.ja: ココナッツミルクが飲みたい。

ex.en: Coconuts grew on my island.
ex.ja: 私の島では、ココナッツが育ちます。

ex.en: We don't have any coconut gel here.
ex.ja: ナタデココはありませんよ。

note.ja: ポルトガル語 coco（お化け・笑った顔）+ nut。実の3つの穴が顔に見えることから。

en: To be made up of; to consist of (especially a comprehensive list of parts).
To compose; to constitute.

comprise.ety: From Middle English comprisen, from Old French compris, past participle of comprendre, from Latin comprehendere, contr. comprendere, past participle comprehensus (“to comprehend”); see comprehend. Compare apprise, reprise, surprise.

ex.en: My house is comprised of these four rooms.
ex.ja: 私の家はこの４つの部屋から成っている。

ex.en: The committee is comprised of ten members.
ex.ja: 委員会は十名で構成されている。

ex.en: The committee comprises ten members.
ex.ja: 委員会は十名で構成されている。

note.ja: com（共に）+ pris（つかむ）+ e。一つにつかみ取る →「〜から成る・〜を構成する」。

en: The open admittance of having done something (especially something bad).
A formal document providing such an admission.

confession.ety:
From Middle English confessioun, from Old French confession, from Latin cōnfessiō, cōnfessiōnem (“confession, acknowledgment, creed or avowal of one's faith”). Displaced native Old English andetnes. Doublet of confessio.
Morphologically confess + -ion.
Sense 6 is a calque of 告白 (kokuhaku).

ex.en: The police forced a confession from her.
ex.ja: 警察は彼女を無理やり白状させた。

note.ja: con（完全に）+ fateri（認める）+ -ion。「すっかり認めること」→「告白・自白」。profess（公言する）、professor も同じ fateri。

en: A narrow hall or passage with rooms leading off it, as in a building or in a railway carriage.
A restricted tract of land that allows passage between two places.

corridor.ety: Borrowed from French corridor, from Italian corridore (“long passage”) (= corridoio), from correre (“to run”).

ex.en: The corridor was so crowded that we couldn't walk.
ex.ja: 廊下は大変混雑していたので歩けなかった。

ex.en: I happened to witness the bullying in the corridor.
ex.ja: 偶然、廊下でいじめを目撃した。

ex.en: The school corridors are always crowded.
ex.ja: 学校の廊下はいつもにぎやかだ。

note.ja: イタリア語 corridore（走る所）から。correre（走る）。「走り抜ける通路」→「廊下」。courier（急使）、current と同じ cur。

en: A reputation impacting one's ability to be believed.
A believability of statements by a witness, as measured by whether the testimony is probable or improbable when judged by common experience.

credibility.ety: Borrowed from French crédibilité, from Medieval Latin credibilitas, from Latin credibilis. By surface analysis, credible + -ity.

ex.en: They've lost all credibility.
ex.ja: 彼らは信憑性を完全に失った。

ex.en: Tom lost his credibility.
ex.ja: トムは信用を失った。

ex.en: He lost his credibility because he betrayed a friend.
ex.ja: 彼は友人を裏切って信用を落とした。

note.ja: cred（信じる）+ ibil + ity。信じられる性質 →「信頼性・信用」。

ex.ja: 突然音がして彼らはゲームから注意をそらした。

en: A carnivorous cetacean, typically with a beak-like snout, famed for their intelligence and occasional willingness to approach humans.
Tursiops truncatus, (Atlantic bottlenose dolphin) the most well-known species.

dolphin.ety: From Middle English delphyn, from Latin delphīnus, from Ancient Greek δελφίς (delphís), from δελφύς (delphús, “womb”); the modern form in -ol- is probably influenced by the pronunciation of Middle French dauphin. Compare Dutch dolfijn and Swedish delfin. Doublet of dauphin. Displaced native Old English mereswīn (literally “sea pig”), whence English mereswine.

ex.en: The boy considered the dolphin his best friend.
ex.ja: 少年はいるかを親友だと思っていた。

ex.en: Tom drew a picture of a dolphin.
ex.ja: トムはイルカの絵を描いた。

ex.en: We took pictures of the dolphins.
ex.ja: イルカの写真を撮りました。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 delphis（イルカ）から。delphys（子宮）と関係し「子を産む魚」の意とされる。

en: A car manufactured by Ferrari.

Ferrari.ety: From Enzo Ferrari, founder of the Ferrari automotive company.

ex.en: Even if I had enough money, I still wouldn't buy a Ferrari.
ex.ja: 私は仮に十分な資金があるとしても、フェラーリは買わないだろうね。

ex.en: I don't want a Ferrari bad enough to sell my house to get one.
ex.ja: 自分の家を売ってまでフェラーリは欲しくないよ。

en: The cardinal number occurring after thirteen and before fifteen.
A group of fourteen items.

fourteen.ety: From Middle English fourtene, from Old English fēowertīene, from Proto-Germanic *fedurtehun. Cognate with West Frisian fjirtjin, Dutch veertien, German vierzehn, Danish fjorten. Equivalent to four + -teen.

ex.en: His car got no more than fourteen miles.
ex.ja: 彼の車は１４マイルしか走れなかった。

ex.en: I've been working since I was fourteen years old.
ex.ja: 14歳の時から働いています。

ex.en: I will be fourteen years old tomorrow.
ex.ja: 私は明日１４才になります。

ex.ja: この章では幾何学の概念に焦点をあてます。

ex.en: We're having an examination in geometry tomorrow.
ex.ja: 明日幾何の試験があります。

en: Someone who likes to talk about other people's private or personal business.
Idle talk about someone’s private or personal matters, especially about someone not present.
To talk about someone else's private or personal business, especially in a manner that spreads the information.
To talk idly.

gossip.ety: From Middle English gossib, godsib (“a close friend or relation, a confidant; a godparent”), from Old English godsibb (“godparent, sponsor”), equivalent to god- + sib (“related”). Doublet of godsib. For sense evolution to "gossip, discussing others' personal affairs," compare French commérage.

ex.en: Hey, is he the one everyone gossips about?
ex.ja: ねえ、あれが噂の？

ex.en: I have no time to engage in gossip.
ex.ja: 噂話のお相手をしている暇はない。

ex.en: She spread the gossip all over the town.
ex.ja: 彼女はそのうわさを町中にふれ回った。

note.ja: 古英語 godsibb ＝ god（神）+ sibb（親族）。「洗礼の名付け親」→ 親しい仲間 → 仲間内のおしゃべり →「うわさ話」。

en: The parent of someone's parent.
Synonym of grandfather.

grandparent.ety: From grand- + parent. Compare French grand-parent.

ex.en: Tom lives in Boston with his grandparents.
ex.ja: トムは祖父と祖母と一緒にボストンに住んでいる。

ex.en: I only speak French with my grandparents.
ex.ja: 私はお爺さんやお婆さんとしかフランス語で喋らない。

ex.en: After their parents died, their grandparents brought them up.
ex.ja: 両親が亡くなった後、祖父母が彼らを育てた。

note.ja: grand（一世代離れた）+ parent（親）。grandfather、grandson と同じ grand。

en: To transport by drawing or pulling, as with horses or oxen, or a motor vehicle.
To draw or pull something heavy.
An act of hauling or pulling, particularly with force; a (violent) pull or tug.
The distance over which something is hauled or transported, especially if long.

haul.ety:
From Middle English hālen, hailen, haulen, halien (“to drag, pull; to draw up”), from Old French haler (“to haul, pull”), from Frankish *halōn (“to drag, fetch, haul”) or Middle Dutch halen (“to drag, fetch, haul”), possibly merging with Old English *halian (“to haul, drag”); all from Proto-Germanic *halōną, *halēną, *hulōną (“to call, fetch, summon”), from Proto-Indo-European *kelh₁- (“to call, cry, summon”). The noun is derived from the verb.
Cognates
The word is cognate with Danish hale (“to haul”), Middle Dutch halen (“to draw, fetch, haul”), Dutch halen (“to fetch, bring, haul”), Old Fris

ex.en: Pipe down, otherwise you will be hauled out.
ex.ja: だまれ、さもないとほうり出されるぞ。

ex.en: The police have hauled in a suspect for questioning.
ex.ja: 警察が容疑者を尋問するために連行していったよ。

ex.en: Please haul on the rope.
ex.ja: その綱を引っ張ってください。

The wood from this tree.

en: Huge, gigantic, very large.
Supremely good.
Immense extent or expanse; immensity.

immense.ety: From Middle English immens, inmens, from Old French immense, from Latin immensus, from in- (“not”) + mensus (“measured”). Compare incommensurable.

ex.en: Technology has given us immense power.
ex.ja: 科学技術は偉大な力を我々に与えてくれた。

ex.en: That play was an immense success.
ex.ja: その劇はすばらしい成功を収めた。

ex.en: She seems to take immense pleasure in playing with children.
ex.ja: 彼女はこどもたちと遊ぶのが非常に好きだ。

note.ja: im（否定）+ mens（測る）+ e。測ることができない →「莫大な・広大な」。

en: To get involved or involve oneself, causing disturbance.
Of waves, to be correlated with each other when overlapped or superposed.

interfere.ety: From Old French entreferir, from entre- + ferir (“to hit, to strike”), itself from the Latin verb ferio.

ex.en: Don't interfere with Tom while he is reading.
ex.ja: トムが本を読んでいるときは邪魔をしてはいけない。

ex.en: Do not interfere with Tom while he is reading.
ex.ja: トムが本を読んでいる間は邪魔をしてはいけない。

ex.en: Don't interfere with matters that do not concern you!
ex.ja: 自分に関わりのないことには口を出すな。

note.ja: 古フランス語 s'entreferir（互いに打ち合う）から。inter（間）+ ferire（打つ）。「間に入って打つ」→「干渉する・邪魔をする」。

en: The junction of two (or more) paths, streets, highways, or other thoroughfares.
Any overlap, confluence, or crossover.

intersection.ety: From Middle French intersection and its etymon Latin intersectiō. By surface analysis, intersect + -ion.

ex.en: He was nearly run over at an intersection.
ex.ja: 彼はあやうく交差点でひかれそうになった。

ex.en: The intersection where the accident happened is near here.
ex.ja: 事故が起きた交差点はこの近くです。

ex.en: Please turn right at the next intersection.
ex.ja: 次の交差点を右に曲がってください。

note.ja: inter（間で）+ sect（切る）+ ion。互いに切り合う所 →「交差点・交わり」。

en: One who investigates.

investigator.ety: Attested in the mid‐16th century; from Latin investigator, from investigare, equivalent to investigate + -or.

ex.en: The crime investigators are looking into the murder case.
ex.ja: 犯罪調査官がこの殺人事件を調べている。

ex.en: Tom used to be a private investigator in Boston.
ex.ja: トムは以前、ボストンで私立探偵をしていた。

ex.en: Investigators are running a probe into what caused the crash.
ex.ja: 調査団は墜落の原因について綿密な調査を行っています。

note.ja: investigate（調査する）+ -or。in（中に）+ vestigium（足跡）。「足跡をたどる人」→「調査員・捜査官」。

en: Young; not fully developed.
Characteristic of youth or immaturity; childish.
A prepubescent child.
A person younger than the age of majority; a minor.

en: The sum total of a person's actions, which determine the person's next incarnation in samsara, the cycle of death and rebirth.
A force or law of nature which causes one to reap what one sows; destiny; fate.

karma.ety: Borrowed from Sanskrit कर्म (kárma), nom.sg. of कर्मन् (kárman, “act, action, performance”); first attested in English in 1785 in a translation of the Bhagavad Gita by Charles Wilkins.

en: A force compounded by means of a lever rotating around a pivot.
Any influence which is compounded or used to gain an advantage.

leverage.ety: From lever + -age. The verb likely comes from martial arts/judo usage, where one would "use an opponent's leverage (i.e. their weight, height, centre of balance, etc.)" against them in order to defeat them.

ex.ja: 投資家グループは、レバレッジドバイアウトを企んでいる。

ex.en: Many conspiracy theorists leverage unverifiable statements and claim them as facts.
ex.ja: 多くの陰謀論者が、未検証な発言を利用してそれらを事実と主張する。

en: The human race in its entirety.
Men collectively, as opposed to all women.

mankind.ety: From Middle English mankynde, alteration (due to kynde = “kind, nature, sort”) of earlier mankyn, from Old English mancynn. Equivalent to man + kin, and/or man + -kind. ex.ja: 平和は人類にとって大事な生存条件です。

ex.en: That can be said of mankind at large.
ex.ja: そのことは人間全般に言える。

ex.en: Cancer is a great enemy of mankind.
ex.ja: 癌は人類の強敵である。

note.ja: man（人）+ kind（種族）。「人という種族」→「人類」。

ex.ja: このチョコレート工場が毎日２０トンのココア原料を使います。

militia.ety:

note.ja: ラテン語 miles（兵士）から。militia（軍務）。「市民による軍隊」→「民兵」。military と同じ。

obstacle.ety: From Middle English obstacle, from Old French obstacle, from Latin obstāculum.

ex.ja: 多くの障害にもめげず前進した。

ex.en: He refused to quit despite many obstacles.
ex.ja: 多くの障害にも関わらず、彼は放棄しなかった。

ex.en: We must go forward getting the better of all obstacles.
ex.ja: 我々はあらゆる障害を排除して進まなければならない。

note.ja: ob（向かって・妨げて）+ stare（立つ）+ -cle。「前に立ちはだかるもの」→「障害」。

Having no prominent or important feature, as of an argument, discourse, etc.

pointless.ety: From Middle English pointles, poynteles, poyntlees. By surface analysis, point + -less.

ex.ja: そんなつまらないことで両親に面倒をかけてはいけない。

ex.ja: 愛のない人生など全く無意味だ。

ex.ja: くだらない話を最後まで聞いてくれてありがとう。

A word, phrase or line supplied by a prompter to an actor who has forgotten the script.
A suggestion for inspiration given to an author.
To lead (someone) toward what they should say or do.
To say (something) in order to help or encourage someone to speak.

The adjective is from Middle English prompte, from Middle French prompt and its etymon Latin prōmptus (“visible, apparent, evident”), past participle of prōmō (“to take or bring out or forth, produce, bring to light”), from prō (“forth, forward”) + emō (“to take, acquire, buy”). Doublet of pronto.

ex.en: He wrote a prompt answer to my letter.
ex.ja: 彼は私の手紙にすぐさま返事を書いてくれた。

ex.en: We look forward to receiving your prompt reply.
ex.ja: あなたからすぐに返事がもらえることを楽しみにしています。

ex.en: Be prompt to do what is asked.
ex.ja: 頼まれた事はすぐにやりなさい。

en: The act or process of qualifying for a position, achievement etc.
An ability or attribute that aids someone's chances of qualifying for something; specifically, completed professional training.

qualification.ety: Borrowed from Middle French qualification in the 1540s, which in turn derives from Medieval Latin quālificātiō. By surface analysis, qual(ify) + -ification.

ex.ja: 一定の条件付きで、彼の提案に賛成します。

ex.ja: その職に就く為にはそれ相応の資格が必要です。

ex.ja: 無条件でその計画に同意した。

To interpret, give an interpretation or rendition of.
Stucco or plaster applied to exterior walls.
Stucco or plaster applied to interior walls.

render.ety: From Middle English renderen, rendren, from Old French rendre (“render, give back”), from Late Latin rendere, from Latin reddere (“make, give back”).

ex.ja: 彼女はその恋歌を非常にうまく表現した。

One who has possession of any place.
To hold as, or be, a tenant.
To inhabit.

ex.en: The tenant must pay the landlord the rent at the end of each month.
ex.ja: 店子は毎月末に大家に家賃を払わなければならない。

note.ja: ten（保つ）+ ant（人）。（土地や建物を）保有している人 →「借家人・テナント」。

en: A flat open area on the topmost floor of a building or apartment
A platform that extends outwards from a building.
To provide something with a terrace.
To form something into a terrace.

terrace.ety: Borrowed from French terrasse, from Old Occitan terrassa, from Vulgar Latin *terrācea, from terra (“land”). Doublet of terrasse.

ex.en: Could we have a table on the terrace?
ex.ja: テラスがいいのですが。

ex.en: You can't smoke except on the terrace.
ex.ja: テラス以外での喫煙は禁止です。

ex.en: Carry all the chairs to the terrace.
ex.ja: 椅子は全部、テラスに持って行って。

note.ja: ラテン語 terra（大地）から。土を盛った台 →「段々畑・テラス」。

en: One who carries out a theft.
One who steals another person's property, especially by stealth and without using force or violence.

thief.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Germanic *þeubaz
Proto-West Germanic *þeub
Old English þēof
Middle English thef
English thief
From Middle English thef, theef, þef, from Old English þēof, from Proto-West Germanic *þeub, from Proto-Germanic *þeubaz. Cognate with Saterland Frisian Tjoof (“thief”), West Frisian tsjeaf (“thief”), Dutch dief (“thief”), Low German Deef, Deev (“thief”), German Dieb (“thief”), Danish tyv (“thief”), Swedish tjuv (“thief”), Icelandic þjófur (“thief”).

ex.en: The dog is trained to watch for thieves.
ex.ja: その犬は泥棒の番をするように訓練されている。

ex.en: I arrested many thieves at the same time.
ex.ja: 私は泥棒を一網打尽に逮捕した。

ex.en: The thieves ran away after it got dark.
ex.ja: 泥棒は暗くなってから逃げた。

note.ja: 古英語 thēof から。ドイツ語 Dieb と同じ。複数形 thieves、theft（盗み）も同じ語。

en: An assembly including one or more judges to conduct judicial business; a court of law.
A kind of village hall used to transact business, to quarter troops and travellers, and to confine prisoners.

tribunal.ety:
PIE word
 *tréyes
From Old French tribunal, from Latin tribūnal (“tribunal”), from tribus (“tribe”).

note.ja: ラテン語 tribunal（護民官の座る壇）から。tribunus（護民官）。「裁きを下す壇」→「法廷」。tribe と同系。

en: Without doubt; definitely.

undoubtedly.ety: From Middle English undoutedly, equivalent to undoubted + -ly.

ex.en: She was undoubtedly a beautiful woman when she was young.
ex.ja: 彼女は若い頃は美人だったに違いない。

ex.en: That's an unusual thing, undoubtedly.
ex.ja: それは全く異例のことだ。

note.ja: un（否定）+ doubt（疑い）+ -ed + -ly。「疑われることなく」→「確かに」。

en: To substantiate or prove the truth of something.
To confirm or test the truth or accuracy of something.

verify.ety: From Old French verifier (French: vérifier), from Medieval Latin vērificāre (“make true”), from Latin vērus (“true”) + faciō (“do, make”); see -fy.

ex.en: Could you verify that your computer is plugged in?
ex.ja: お客様のパソコンのプラグが電源に差し込まれているか確認してくださいませんか？

ex.en: Please verify that your username and password have been entered correctly.
ex.ja: ユーザー名とパスワードが正しく入力されていることを確認してください。

note.ja: ver（真実）+ ify（〜にする）。真実だと確かめる →「確認する・立証する」。

en: A vile, wicked person.
An extremely depraved person, or one capable or guilty of great crimes.

villain.ety:
Probably from Middle English vilein, from Old French vilein (modern French vilain), in turn from Late Latin vīllānus, meaning serf or peasant, someone who is bound to the soil of a Latin vīlla, which is to say, worked on the equivalent of a plantation in late Antiquity, in Italy or Gaul. Doublet of villein.
Compare typologically pagan (see more).

ex.en: One murder makes a villain, millions a hero.
ex.ja: 一人殺せば悪人となるが何百万人を殺せば英雄となる。

note.ja: ラテン語 villanus（農場の使用人）から。villa（農場の屋敷）。「農奴」→「卑しい者」→「悪党・悪役」と意味が悪くなった。village も同じ villa。

en: A device designed to be placed in the mouth and blown, or driven by steam or some other mechanism, to make a whistling sound.
An act of whistling.
To make a shrill, high-pitched sound by forcing air through the mouth. To produce a whistling sound, restrictions to the flow of air are …
To make a similar sound by forcing air through a musical instrument or a pipe etc.

whistle.ety: From Middle English whistel, whistil, whistle, from Old English hwistle, from the verb (see below).

ex.en: On hearing the whistle, they started at full speed.
ex.ja: ホイッスルの音を聞くやいなや、彼らは全速力で走りだした。

ex.en: Do you know how to whistle?
ex.ja: 口笛の吹き方ってわかる？

ex.en: He whistled as he went along.
ex.ja: 彼は歩きながら口笛を吹いた。

note.ja: 古英語 hwistlian から。擬音的な語。「ヒュー」という音。

en: Happening once every year.
Over the course of one year.
Once a year.
Every year.
Something that is published once a year.

yearly.ety: From Middle English yeerly, yerely, from Old English ġēarlīċ, ġērlīċ (“yearly, of the year, annual”), equivalent to year + -ly (adjectival suffix) or -ly (adverbial suffix). Cognate with Scots yerelie (“yearly”), Saterland Frisian jierelk (“yearly”), West Frisian jierliks (“yearly”), Dutch jaarlijks (“yearly”), Afrikaans jaarliks (“yearly”), German jährlich (“yearly”), Danish årlig (“yearly”), Norwegian Bokmål årlig (“yearly”), Norwegian Nynorsk årleg (“yearly”), Swedish årlig (“yearly”), Icelandic árlegur (“yearly”).

ex.en: I worked on a yearly contract.
ex.ja: 私は１年契約で働いた。

ex.en: I visit the city yearly.
ex.ja: 私は年に一度その都市を訪れます。

note.ja: year（年）+ -ly。「毎年の」。

en: Prone to treat someone badly by coarse, insulting words or other maltreatment; vituperative; reproachful; scurrilous.
Being physically or emotionally injurious; characterized by repeated violence or other abuse.

abusive.ety: First attested in the 1530s. From French abusif, from Latin abūsīvus, from abusus + -ivus (“-ive”). Equivalent to abuse + -ive.

ex.en: I had never received such an abusive letter before.
ex.ja: 私はそれまでにこれほど罵倒にみちた手紙を受け取ったことはなかった。

ex.en: He was charged with the crime of abusive language.
ex.ja: 彼は暴言罪で告発された。

ex.en: They used abusive language to her.
ex.ja: 彼らは彼女を口汚なくののしった。

en: A narrow street or passageway, especially one through the middle of a block giving access to the rear of lots of buildings.
The area between the outfielders.

alley.ety: From Middle English aleye, from Anglo-Norman aleie, feminine of alé, past participle of aler (“to go”) (French aller). Doublet of allée.

ex.en: Watch your step in dark alleys.
ex.ja: 暗い道では足元に気をつけなさい。

ex.en: It is right up his alley.
ex.ja: 彼にはそんなことはお手の物だ。

ex.en: This is a dead-end alley.
ex.ja: この路地は通り抜けできません。

note.ja: 古フランス語 alee（通路）から。aller（行く）。「歩いて行く道」→「路地」。

en: A desire to eat food or consume drinks.
Any strong desire; an eagerness or longing.

appetite.ety: From Middle English appetit, from Old French apetit (French appétit), from Latin appetitus, from appetere (“to strive after, long for”); ad + petere (“to seek”). See petition, and compare with appetence.

ex.en: Tom had no appetite because of his illness.
ex.ja: トムは病気のため食欲がなかった。

ex.en: He had no appetite because of the heat.
ex.ja: 彼は暑さのために食欲がなかった。

ex.en: He has little appetite for lack of exercise.
ex.ja: 彼は運動不足であまり食欲がない。

note.ja: ap（〜へ）+ pet（求める）+ ite。何かを求めること →「食欲・欲求」。

en: A yard to the rear of a house or similar residence.
A person's neighborhood, or an area nearby to a person's usual residence or place of work and where the person is likely to go.

ex.en: My backyard can hold more than ten people.
ex.ja: 家の裏庭なら１０人以上入れるわよ。

ex.en: Tom has a tree in his backyard.
ex.ja: トムの家の裏庭には木があります。

ex.en: There's a possibility that Tom is in the backyard.
ex.ja: トムは裏庭にいるかもしれません。

note.ja: back（裏）+ yard（庭）。yard はもと「囲い地」で garden と同じ祖先。

en: A very large outdoor sign, generally used for advertising.
A piece of thick plank, armed with iron plates, and fixed on the bow or fore-channels of a vessel, for the bill or fluke of the anchor to…
To advertise on a billboard.

note.ja: bill（貼り紙・ビラ）+ board（板）。「ビラを貼る板」→「広告板」。bill はラテン語 bulla（封印・文書）。

en: A person who is intentionally physically or emotionally cruel to others, especially to those whom they perceive as being vulnerable or of…
A noisy, blustering, tyrannical person, more insolent than courageous; one who is threatening and quarrelsome.
To intimidate (someone) as a bully.
To act aggressively towards.
Well done; often sarcastic in modern use.

bully.ety:
From 1530, as a term of endearment, probably a diminutive ( + -y) of Dutch boel (“lover; brother”), from Middle Dutch boel, boele (“brother; lover”), from Old Dutch *buolo, from Proto-Germanic *bōlô (compare Middle Low German bôle (“brother”), Middle High German buole (“brother; close relative; close relation”) (whence German Buhle (“lover”)), Old English Bōla, Bōlla (personal name), diminutive of expressive *bō- (“brother, father”). Compare also Latvian bālinš (“brother”). More at boy.
The term acquired a negative connotation during the 17th century; first ‘noisy, blustering fellow’ then ‘a p

ex.en: Pick on somebody your own size, you bully.
ex.ja: 弱いものいじめはよせ、このごろつきめが！

ex.en: Tom committed suicide because he was bullied at school.
ex.ja: トムは学校でのいじめが原因で自殺した。

ex.en: He just loves to bully people.
ex.ja: 彼は弱いものいじめが好きなのです。

note.ja: オランダ語 boel（恋人・兄弟）から。「いい人」→「威張る人」→「いじめっ子」と意味が悪くなった。

en: The act or process of calculating.
The result of calculating.

calculation.ety: From Middle English calculation, borrowed from Latin calculatio, calculationis. Morphologically calculate + -ion.

ex.en: Have you allowed for any error in your calculation?
ex.ja: 計算にいくらかの誤差を考慮に入れましたか。

ex.en: I'm not an idiot. I'm just not good at calculations.
ex.ja: 馬鹿じゃないのよ。計算が苦手なだけよ。

ex.en: There are a lot of results and a calculation mistakes.
ex.ja: 結果、計算ミスが多い。

note.ja: calculate（計算する）+ -ion。ラテン語 calculus（小石）。昔は小石で数を数えた →「計算」。calcium（石灰）と同系。

en: To have a child; to become pregnant (with).
To develop; to form in the mind; to imagine.

conceive.ety: From Middle English conceyven, from Old French concevoir, conceveir, from Latin concipiō, concipere (“to devise, to conceive”).

ex.en: No one conceived his words to be important.
ex.ja: だれも彼の言葉を重要なものと思わなかった。

ex.en: They conceived a plan to surprise the enemy.
ex.ja: 彼らは敵をびっくりさせる計画を思いついた。

ex.en: I conceived of the plan while I was smoking.
ex.ja: 私はタバコを吸っている間にその計画を思いついた。

note.ja: con（共に）+ ceiv（つかむ・取る）+ e。心の中に取り込む →「思いつく・想像する・妊娠する」。concept（概念）。

en: that has been disintegrated in a solvent

ex.en: It's likely the Diet will be dissolved.
ex.ja: 国会は解散するだろう。

ex.en: My resolution dissolved at the last moment.
ex.ja: いざというとき決意がくじけた。

ex.en: He dissolved some sugar in his coffee.
ex.ja: 彼はコーヒーに砂糖を溶かした。

en: A series of rulers or dynasts from one family.
A family considered over time, with its ancestors and descendants

dynasty.ety: Borrowed from Middle French dynastie, from Late Latin dynastia, from Ancient Greek δυναστεία (dunasteía, “power, dominion”).

ex.en: The Tudor Dynasty fell in the year 1603.
ex.ja: チューダー朝は１６０３年に崩壊した。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 dynasteia（支配力）から。dynamis（力）。「支配する一族」→「王朝」。dynamic、dynamite も同じ。

en: An expert in economics, especially one who studies economic data and extracts higher-level information or proposes theories.
One concerned with political economy.

economist.ety: From Middle French économiste (“household manager”). By surface analysis, economy + -ist.

ex.en: This problem has been debated by many economists.
ex.ja: この問題は多くの経済学者によって論じられてきた。

ex.en: Many economists are ignorant of that fact.
ex.ja: 多くの経済学者はその事実に気づいていない。

ex.en: The economist instinctively anticipated the current depression.
ex.ja: その経済学者は現在の不況を本能的に予期していた。

note.ja: economy（経済）+ -ist。ギリシャ語 oikonomia ＝ oikos（家）+ nomos（管理）。「家計の管理」→「経済」。

en: Flanked by endorses.
In an extensive manner, widely.
To a great extent.

extensively.ety:
Etymology tree
Late Latin extensīvusder.
Middle English extensive
English extensive
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English extensively
From extensive + -ly.

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ tens（伸ばす）+ ive + ly。広く伸ばして →「広範囲に・大規模に」。

en: The part of the face above the eyebrows and below the hairline.
confidence; audacity; impudence.

forehead.ety: From Middle English forhed, forheed, from Old English forehēafod, from Proto-West Germanic *forēhaubid, corresponding to fore- + head. Cognate with Scots foreheid (“forehead”), Dutch voorhoofd (“forehead”), German Vorhaupt (“forehead”), Danish forhoved (“brow; forehead; face”). Compare also West Frisian foarholle (“forehead”), German Low German Vörkopp (“forehead”).

ex.en: Tom gave Mary a kiss on the forehead.
ex.ja: トムはメアリーの額にキスをした。

ex.en: He put his hand to his forehead.
ex.ja: 彼は額に手を当てた。

ex.en: He was lost in thought with his hand on his forehead.
ex.ja: 彼は額に手を当てて物思いにふけった。

note.ja: fore（前）+ head（頭）。「頭の前の部分」→「額」。

en: A person from a foreign country.
A private job run by an employee at a trade factory rather than going through the business.

foreigner.ety: From Middle English forner, foreyner, foroner, forenere, augmentation of earlier forein (“foreigner”), from the adjective. Equivalent to foreign + -er. Use of the -er suffix may be due to analogy with Middle English straunger (“stranger”). Displaced native Old English elþēodiġ.

ex.en: This school has several foreigners on the roll.
ex.ja: この学校には数人の外国人が在籍している。

ex.en: It is hard for foreigners to learn Japanese.
ex.ja: 日本語は外人にとって覚えにくい。

ex.en: A foreigner asked me where the station was.
ex.ja: ある外国人が私に駅がどこにあるかと聞いた。

note.ja: foreign（外国の）+ -er。ラテン語 foras（戸の外に）から。g は綴りに入った飾りで発音しない。

en: The action of forgiving.
A readiness to forgive.

ex.ja: 私は間違ってすみませんと謝った。

ex.ja: 彼女は非難されるようなことをしたのを許してほしいと言った。

ex.en: The princess begged forgiveness from the emperor.
ex.ja: 姫君は皇帝に寛恕を請いました。

note.ja: forgive（許す）+ -ness。for（すっかり）+ give（与える）。「（罪を）すっかり与えてしまう」→「許す」。

en: A precious stone, usually of substantial monetary value or prized for its beauty or shine.
Any precious or highly valued thing or person.
To adorn with, or as if with, gems.

gem.ety: Inherited from Middle English gemme, gimme, yimme, ȝimme, from Old English ġimm, from Proto-West Germanic *gimmu (“gem”) and Old French gemme (“gem”), both from Latin gemma (“a swelling bud; jewel, gem”). Doublet of gemma and Gemma.

ex.en: At last, the gem was in his hands.
ex.ja: ついに彼はその宝石を手に入れた。

ex.en: The crown was set with gems.
ex.ja: その王冠は宝石で飾られていた。

ex.en: It's not as if just anybody can write a literary gem.
ex.ja: 誰もが名文を書けるわけではない。

note.ja: ラテン語 gemma（芽・宝石）から。「芽のように輝く石」→「宝石・逸品」。

en: Of a location, frequented by a ghost or ghosts.
Obsessed (by an idea, threat, etc.).

ex.en: That old house is thought to be haunted.
ex.ja: あの古い家には良くお化けが出るそうだ。

ex.en: They say that old house is haunted.
ex.ja: あの古い家には幽霊が出るそうだ。

ex.en: The house is said to be haunted.
ex.ja: その家には幽霊が出るといわれる。

note.ja: haunt（出没する）+ -ed。古フランス語 hanter（よく訪れる）から。「（幽霊が）よく現れる」→「幽霊の出る」。

en: An evergreen plant, Calluna vulgaris, with spiky leaves and small purple, pink, or white flowers.
A plant in the family Ericaceae.
Of a purple colour with a tint of pink and blue.

heather.ety: From Middle English hather, hathir, from Old English *hǣddre and hǣþ (“heather”), cognate with Scots hedder, hadder, heddir (“heather”), Saterland Frisian Heede (“heather”), West Frisian heide (“heather”), Dutch heide (“heather”), German Low German Heide, Heid (“heather”), German Heide (“heather”).

note.ja: スコットランドの荒れ地に咲く小さな花（ヒースの一種）。語源ははっきりしない。

en: A tentative conjecture explaining an observation, phenomenon or scientific problem and that can be tested by further observation, investi…
An assumption taken to be true for the purpose of argument or investigation.

hypothesis.ety: Recorded since 1596, from Middle French hypothese, from Late Latin hypothesis, from Ancient Greek ὑπόθεσις (hupóthesis, “base, basis of an argument, supposition”, literally “a placing under”), itself from ὑποτίθημι (hupotíthēmi, “to set before, suggest”), from ὑπό (hupó, “below”) + τίθημι (títhēmi, “to put, place”). Compare hypothec.

ex.en: These facts bear out my hypothesis.
ex.ja: これらの事実は私の仮説の裏付けになる。

ex.en: The facts bear out this hypothesis.
ex.ja: 諸事実がこの仮説を実証している。

ex.en: This data supports the hypothesis.
ex.ja: これらのデータはその仮説を支持している。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 hypo（下に）+ thesis（置くこと）。「議論の下に置くもの」→「仮説」。thesis（論文）も同じ。

en: In a manner contrary to law.

ex.en: If you continue staying here illegally, the police will catch you.
ex.ja: 不法滞在を続ければ、警察につかまります。

ex.en: A lot of bicycles are illegally parked in front of the station.
ex.ja: 駅前には多くの自転車が違法に止められています。

note.ja: il（否定）+ legal（合法の）+ -ly。legal はラテン語 lex（法）。「法に反して」。

Having a tendency, preference, likelihood, or disposition.

ex.ja: われわれは彼を支持したい気がする。

ex.ja: 彼のアドバイスで考えを変える気になった。

ex.en: I don't feel inclined to play baseball today.
ex.ja: 今日は野球をやる気がしないんだ。

en: Not formal or ceremonious.
Not in accord with the usual regulations.

ex.ja: 私のアメリカのクラスはそんなに形式ばっていません。

ex.en: It was only an informal party.
ex.ja: ほんの気楽なパーティーだった。

ex.en: It's quite an informal meeting.
ex.ja: ごく内輪の集まりなのです。

note.ja: in（否定）+ formal（正式の）。「形式ばらない・非公式の」。form（形）。

A scorekeeper, especially one who tallies billiard scores.
To mark or write on (something) using a marker

ex.en: They got through the marsh.

en: A high-ranking officer in the household of a medieval prince or lord, who was originally in charge of the cavalry and later the military …
A military officer of the highest rank in several countries, including France and the former Soviet Union; equivalent to a general of the…
To arrange (troops, etc.) in line for inspection or a parade.
To arrange (facts, etc.) in some methodical order.

marshal.ety: From Middle English marschal, from Anglo-Norman mareschal (“farrier; military commander”), from Medieval Latin mariscalcus (“groom, army commander, court dignitary”), either from Frankish *marhaskalk, or Old High German marah-scalc (“horse-servant”), from Proto-West Germanic *marh + *skalk (whence Old Saxon maraskalk, marahscalc). Compare English mare + shalk.

note.ja: 古フランス語 mareschal（馬の世話係）から。ゲルマン系 marh（馬）+ scalc（召使い）。「馬丁」→「軍の高官・元帥」→「保安官」と出世した語。

en: The state of being mature, ready or ripe; the prime state of productibility and self expression.
When bodily growth has completed and/or reproduction can begin.

maturity.ety: From Middle English maturitee, maturyte, from Old French maturité, from Latin mātūritātem. By surface analysis, mature + -ity.

ex.en: Willingness to take responsibility is a sign of maturity.
ex.ja: 進んで責任を取るということは成熟の印である。

ex.en: With this type of insurance, most policies don't come with a maturity refund.
ex.ja: この種の保険は掛け捨てが多い。

note.ja: mature（成熟した）+ -ity。ラテン語 maturus（熟した・時宜を得た）。「成熟」→（手形の）「満期」。premature（早すぎる）も同じ。

en: In a disorderly state; chaotic; disorderly.
Prone to causing mess.

ex.ja: 髪がめちゃくちゃ！！

ex.ja: 今日部屋の掃除したばかりなのに、なんでこんなに散らかってるの？

ex.en: If I don't take care of my fur, it gets really messy.
ex.ja: 毛繕いしないと、ボサボサになっちゃうんだ。

note.ja: mess（散らかり）+ -y。mess はもと「料理の一皿」→ ごちゃまぜの食べ物 →「散らかり」。

en: One trained in ninjutsu, especially one used for espionage, assassination, and other tasks requiring stealth during Japan's shogunate per…
One who very skillful, considered similar to the historical ninja, especially in covert or stealthy operation.
Fast and sneaky.
To act or move like a ninja, particularly with regard to a combination of speed, power, and stealth.

ninja.ety:

The Juggalo slang sense arose via influence from AAVE nigga.

ex.en: My older sister is a female ninja.
ex.ja: 僕の姉はくノ一なんです。

ex.ja: トムが忍者のような格好してるよ。

ex.en: Let's make believe we're ninjas.
ex.ja: 忍者ごっこをしよう。

note.ja: 日本語「忍者」がそのまま英語になった語。

A person seen as having owl-like characteristics, especially appearing wise or serious, or being nocturnally active.

ex.en: The owl can see in the dark.
ex.ja: ふくろうは暗闇で目が見える。

ex.ja: フクロウはとても賢いと考えられている。

ex.ja: フクロウは、ゆっくり歩く。

en: A place where prescription drugs are sold or dispensed.
The science of medicinal substances, inclusive of pharmaceutics, pharmaceutical chemistry, pharmacology, phytochemistry, and forensics.

pharmacy.ety: From Middle English pharmacy, borrowed from Middle French pharmacie (“the art of creating drugs; a drug, especially a laxative”), from Old French farmacie, from Medieval Latin pharmacia, from Ancient Greek φαρμακεία (pharmakeía, “the use of drugs”), from φάρμακον (phármakon, “a drug, charm, enchantment”), of uncertain but likely Pre-Greek origin. Attested since late 14th century.

ex.en: Until what time does your pharmacy stay open?
ex.ja: 薬局は何時まで開いていますか。

ex.en: I go to the pharmacy and buy medicine.
ex.ja: 薬局へ行って薬を買う。

ex.en: This medicine is not sold yet in pharmacies.
ex.ja: この薬はまだ薬局で売られていない。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 pharmakon（薬）から。「薬を作る所」→「薬局・薬学」。pharmaceutical も同じ。

en: Difficult to overcome, solve, or decide.
Not settled, uncertain, of uncertain outcome; debatable, questionable, open to doubt.
A problem or difficulty in a particular field of study.

problematic.ety: Borrowed from Middle French problématique, from Late Latin problematicus, from Ancient Greek προβληματικός (problēmatikós), from πρόβλημα (próblēma, “outjutting, barrier, problem”), from προβάλλω (probállō, “I throw, place before”), from πρό (pró, “before”) + βάλλω (bállō, “I throw, place”). By surface analysis, problem + -atic.

ex.en: The separation of gold from sand is problematic.
ex.ja: 砂から金をより分けるのは難問だ。

en: A person or institution who processes things (foods, photos, applications, etc.).
A device which processes, which changes something (a computer processor, food processor, etc.).

ex.en: I have the same word-processor as this.
ex.ja: 私はこれと同じワープロを持っている。

ex.en: They're always having trouble with their word processor.
ex.ja: 彼らはワープロにいつも手を焼いている。

ex.en: I would like to use your word processor.
ex.ja: あなたのワープロを使いたいのですが。

note.ja: process（処理する）+ -or。pro（前へ）+ cedere（進む）。「進めていくもの」→「処理装置」。proceed、procedure と同じ。

Of or relating to promotion to a post of higher status.
An advertising promotion

en: Likely or expected to happen or become.
Anticipated in the near or far future.
A prospective (potential) member, student, employee, date, partner, etc.

prospective.ety: From Middle French prospectif, from Late Latin prospectivus. See more at English prospect.

ex.en: The company invited their prospective customers to the party.
ex.ja: その会社は将来お得意先になりそうな人々をパーティーに招待した。

ex.ja: 有望な買い手は、契約内容をよく理解できませんでした。

ex.ja: 体重増加は特定の精神薬によくある副作用である。

en: To cancel, invalidate, annul.
To recall; to summon (a person) again; to bring (a person) back from exile or banishment.
An act or instance of repealing.

repeal.ety: From Anglo-Norman repeler, from Old French rapeler (“to call back, call in, call after, revoke”), from Latin repellō (“drive or thrust back”), from re- and pellō (“push or strike”). Doublet of repel.

note.ja: 古フランス語 rapeler（呼び戻す）から。re（元へ）+ appeal（呼びかける）。「呼び戻す」→「（法律を）廃止する」。

en: To cook food by heating in an oven or over a fire without covering, resulting in a crisp, possibly even slightly charred appearance.
To cook by surrounding with hot embers, ashes, sand, etc.
A piece of meat suited to roasting; meat that has been roasted.
A meal consisting of roast foods.
Having been cooked by roasting.
Subjected to roasting; bantered; severely criticized.

roast.ety:
From Middle English rosten, a borrowing from Old French rostir (“to roast, to torture with fire”), from Frankish *rōstijan (“to roast, broil”), from Proto-Germanic *raustijaną (“to roast”), from Proto-Indo-European *Hrews- (“to crackle; roast”). Cognate with Saterland Frisian rosterje (“to roast”), Dutch roosten, roosteren (“to roast”), German rösten (“to roast”).
Displaced native Middle English breden, bræden (“to roast”), from Old English brǣdan, related to German braten (“to roast, grill”).
The noun is from Middle English roste, from Old French rost, roste, from the verb.

ex.en: Roast chicken is one of my favorite dishes.
ex.ja: ローストチキンは大好きな料理の１つです。

ex.en: The fowls were well roasted by the cook.
ex.ja: 鳥は料理人がほどよく焼いた。

ex.en: This meat is roasted well.
ex.ja: この肉はよく焼けている。

note.ja: 古フランス語 rostir（あぶる）から。ゲルマン系で「焼き網」の意。

en: Refuse, waste, garbage, junk, trash.
An item, or items, of low quality.
Exceedingly bad; awful.
Used to express that something is exceedingly bad, awful, or terrible.
Used to express that what was recently said is nonsense or untrue; balderdash!, nonsense!
To criticize, to denigrate, to denounce, to disparage.
To litter.

rubbish.ety: Inherited from Middle English robous (“rubbish, building rubble”), further origin uncertain; possibly from Anglo-Norman rubous, rubouse, rubbouse (“refuse, waste material; building rubble”), and compare Anglo-Latin rebbussa, robousa, robusium, robusum, rubisum, rubusa, rubusium (although the Anglo-Norman and Anglo-Latin words may be derived from the English word instead of the other way around, as there are no known Old French cognates of the word). The English word may be related to rubble, though the connection is unclear. Possibly derived ultimately from Old Norse rubba (“to huddle, crowd t

ex.en: Get the rubbish out of the building.
ex.ja: この建物からガラクタを運び出してくれ。

ex.en: Burn this rubbish on the fire.
ex.ja: このガラクタは火に燃やしなさい。

ex.en: They looked at the rubbish, then they looked at each other.
ex.ja: ガラクタを見て、彼らは互いに顔を見合わせました。

note.ja: 古フランス語 robeux（くず）から。rubble（がれき）と同系とされる。「ごみ・くだらないこと」。

en: A large room, especially one used to receive and entertain guests.
A gathering of people for a social or intellectual meeting.

salon.ety: Borrowed from French salon (“reception room”), from Middle French, from Italian salone (“large hall”), augmented form of sala (“hall”), from Lombardic sala (“room, house, entrance hall”), from Proto-Germanic *salą (“dwelling, house, hall”), from Proto-Indo-European *sel- (“human settlement, village, dwelling”). Cognate with Old High German sal (“room, house, entrance hall”), Old English sæl (“room, hall, castle”), Old Church Slavonic село (selo, “courtyard, village”), Lithuanian sala (“island”). Doublet of saloon.

ex.en: There are three beauty salons on this street.
ex.ja: この街にはエステティックサロンが３軒ある。

ex.en: There's a beauty salon next to the station.
ex.ja: 美容院は駅の横にあります。

ex.en: She goes to the beauty salon at least once a week.
ex.ja: 彼女は少なくとも週一回美容院へ行く。

note.ja: イタリア語 salone（大広間）から。sala（部屋）+ 拡大。「広間」→「サロン・美容院」。saloon（酒場）も同じ。

en: The cardinal number occurring after sixteen and before eighteen, represented in Roman numerals as XVII and in Arabic numerals as 17.

seventeen.ety:
Inherited from Middle English seventene, from Old English seofontīene, from Proto-Germanic *sebuntehun. Cognate with Dutch zeventien, West Frisian santjin, German siebzehn, Danish sytten.
Equivalent to seven + -teen

ex.en: She will be seventeen years old next February.
ex.ja: 彼女は今度の２月で１７歳になる。

ex.en: She got married at the age of seventeen.
ex.ja: 彼女は１７歳の時に結婚した。

ex.en: The class was made up of seventeen children.
ex.ja: そのクラスは１７名の子供から成り立っていた。

en: That which remains when use or need is satisfied, or when a limit is reached; excess; overplus; overage.
Specifically, an amount in the public treasury at any time greater than is required for the ordinary purposes of the government.
Being or constituting a surplus; more than sufficient.
To treat as surplus to requirements; to sell off or dismiss from employment, etc.

surplus.ety: From Middle English surplus, from Middle French surplus. Compare French surplus.

ex.en: There will be a surplus of personnel.
ex.ja: 人員に余剰が出る

ex.ja: 日本では米が、ヨーロッパではワインが余っている。

ex.ja: 日本の貿易黒字は史上最高を記録しました。

en: To cause (food, drink etc.) to pass from the mouth into the stomach; to take into the stomach through the throat.
To take (something) in so that it disappears; to consume, absorb.
The amount swallowed in one gulp; the act of swallowing.
The opening in a pulley block between the sheave and shell through which the rope passes.

swallow.ety:

The noun is

ex.en: He swallowed his anger and went on working.
ex.ja: 彼は怒りを我慢して仕事を続けた。

ex.en: Swallows fly away at the approach of winter.
ex.ja: ツバメは冬が近づくと飛び去る。

ex.en: Many swallows will come soon from the south.
ex.ja: たくさんのツバメがまもなく南からやってくる。

note.ja: 「飲み込む」は古英語 swelgan から。「ツバメ」は古英語 swealwe からで別語。

en: Carried out according to a planned, ordered procedure.
Methodical; regular and orderly.
systematically

systematic.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin systēmaticus, from Koine Greek συστηματικός (sustēmatikós), from σύστημᾰ (sústēmă, “a composite; system”) + -ῐκός (-ĭkós, adjective suffix). Cognate with French systématique and Italian sistematico. By surface analysis, system + -atic.

ex.en: He decided to perform systematic research.
ex.ja: 彼は系統立った調査を行うことにした。

en: Unsatisfactory; not acceptable.
Not conforming to accepted usage.
Something that is not acceptable.

unacceptable.ety: From Middle English unacceptabylle, equivalent to un- + acceptable.

ex.en: This score is unacceptable.
ex.ja: こんな点数じゃだめ。

ex.en: This is totally unacceptable.
ex.ja: こんなことは許されない。

ex.en: It is highly regrettable that your request was considered to be unacceptable.
ex.ja: ご提案を受け入れることができず、たいへん残念です。

note.ja: un（否定）+ accept（受け入れる）+ -able。accept は ad（〜に）+ capere（取る）。「受け入れられない」。

en: In motion, in progress; being done or carried out; on a journey.
A road, track, path, or street for going under another way or obstacle; an underpass.
An underground passage, subway, tunnel.

underway.ety: Calque of Dutch onderweg (“underway”), equivalent to under- + way. Compare also German unterwegs.

ex.ja: 省エネルギーの全国運動が展開中だ。

ex.ja: パーティーを始めようぜ。

en: Not stable.
Having a strong tendency to change.
To release (an animal) from a stable.

unstable.ety: From Middle English unstable; equivalent to un- (“not”) + stable. Piecewise doublet of instable and astable.

ex.en: The weather in April is unstable.
ex.ja: 4月の天気は不安定です。

ex.en: Future prospects for ASEAN seem unstable, no matter how you look at it.

coral.ety: From Old French coral (French corail), from Latin corallium, from Ancient Greek κοράλλιον (korállion, “coral”). stunt.ety: Unknown. Compare Middle Low German stunt (“a shoulder grip with which you throw someone on their back”), Middle English stunt (“foolish; stupid”).

ex.en: That's just a cheap publicity stunt.
ex.ja: それは売名行為だ。

ex.en: The clown's stunts were highly amusing to the boys.
ex.ja: 道化の妙技は少年達にとってとても楽しかった。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。19世紀アメリカで「離れ業」の意味に。「成長を妨げる」は古英語 stunt（愚かな・短い）からで別語。

en: All the electromagnetic radiation given off by the Sun; especially, that in the visible spectrum and that bathes the Earth.
Brightness, hope; a positive outlook.
To work on the side (at a secondary job) during the daytime.

sunlight.ety: From Middle English sonnelight, sunneliht, from Old English sunnan lēoht (“sunlight”), equivalent to sun + light. Cognate with Dutch zonlicht (“sunlight”), German Low German Sünnenlücht (“sunlight”), German Sonnenlicht (“sunlight”).

ex.en: Keep in a place out of direct sunlight.
ex.ja: 直射日光の当たる場所は避けて保管してください。

ex.en: You should protect your eyes from direct sunlight.
ex.ja: 直射日光から目を守った方がいい。

ex.en: Avoid direct sunlight and store at room temperature.
ex.ja: 直射日光を避け、常温で保存してください。

note.ja: sun（太陽）+ light（光）。「日光」。

en: Waves that break on an ocean shoreline.
An instance or session of riding a surfboard in the surf.
To ride a wave on a surfboard; to pursue or take part in the sport of surfing.
To surf at a specified place.

surf.ety:
Probably from earlier suff, suffe (“the inrush of the sea towards the shore”), possibly from Middle English suffe. Compare sough, surf (“a gutter, drain, sewer, trench”) and sough (“a soothing, gentle, murmuring sound of wind or water”). Alternatively, possibly of Indo-Aryan origin, as the word was formerly a reference to the coast of India, though this is doubtful as no positive etymon can be identified.
The verb is from 1917.
The verb referring to "browsing the Internet" was popularized by Jean Armour Polly.

ex.en: When was the last time you went surfing?
ex.ja: 最後にサーフィンに行ったのって、いつ？

ex.en: Did you have a good time swimming and surfing?
ex.ja: 水泳をしたりサーフィンをしたりして楽しかったですか。

ex.en: I surfed the net late last night.
ex.ja: 昨日の夜、遅くまでインターネットしていたの。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。もとは「打ち寄せる波」。→「波乗りをする」→ 波に乗るように見て回る →「ネットサーフィン」。

en: Pertaining to a symbol.
Implicitly representing or referring to another thing.

symbolic.ety: From French symbolique or directly from Latin symbolicus, from Ancient Greek συμβολικός (sumbolikós, “of or belonging to a symbol”), equivalent to symbol + -ic.

ex.en: The dismissal of foreign minister Tanaka is symbolic of the continuing political turmoil.
ex.ja: 田中前外相の更迭に続く政治混乱がその象徴である。

note.ja: symbol（象徴）+ -ic。ギリシャ語 symbolon（割り符）＝ syn（共に）+ ballein（投げる）。「合わせて照合するしるし」→「象徴」。

en: A person who is subject to, liable for, or pays tax.

ex.en: I want to work from the taxpayers' point of view.
ex.ja: 納税者の目線で努力を致したいと思います。

ex.en: All taxpayers have the right to know where their money goes.
ex.ja: 納税者は払った金の行方を知る権利がある。

ex.en: Each taxpayer has the right to know where his money goes.
ex.ja: 納税者は払った金の行方を知る権利がある。

note.ja: tax（税）+ payer（払う人）。tax はラテン語 taxare（評価する）。

en: To provoke someone to do wrong, especially by promising a reward; to entice.
To attract; to allure.

tempt.ety: From Middle English tempten, from Old French tempter (French: tenter), from Latin temptare, from tentare (“to handle, touch, try, test, tempt”), frequentative of tendere (“to stretch”). Displaced native English costning (“temptation”).

ex.en: She was tempted to come with me.
ex.ja: 彼女は私のお供をするように仕向けられた。

ex.en: I am tempted to doubt your friendship.
ex.ja: 私は君の友情を疑いたくなる。

ex.en: What tempted him to come home?
ex.ja: 何が彼を帰宅する気にさせたのか。

note.ja: ラテン語 temptare（試す・さぐる）から。「試してそそのかす」→「誘惑する」。attempt（試みる）も同じ。

en: An attack made by moving the sword parallel to its length and landing with the point.
A push, stab, or lunge forward.
To make advance with force.
To force something upon someone.

thrust.ety: From Middle English þrusten, from Old Norse þrysta, from Proto-Germanic *þrustijaną, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *trewd-.

ex.en: I thrust my hand into my pocket.
ex.ja: 私はポケットに手を突っ込んだ。

ex.en: He thrust the money into his pocket.
ex.ja: 彼はポケットにそのお金を押し込んだ。

ex.en: Don't thrust your knife into the cheese.
ex.ja: チーズの中へナイフを突き刺したりするな。

note.ja: 北欧語 þrýsta（押す）から。threat（脅し）と同系とされる。「強く押す」→「推進力・要点」。

note.ja: tri（3つ）+ log（言葉・物語）+ y。3つの物語 →「三部作」。

Designed for use by wheelchairbound people.
To move using a wheelchair.

ex.ja: 電動車椅子って免許要るの？

ex.ja: トムに車いすは必要なかった。

note.ja: wheel（車輪）+ chair（いす）。「車輪付きのいす」。

en: The act of accusing.
A formal charge brought against a person in a court of law.

accusation.ety: First attested in the late 14th century. ex.ja: 彼女はこれらの告発に対して自らを弁護するためにここへ来たわけではない。

ex.en: She didn't come here to defend herself against these accusations.
ex.ja: 彼女はこれらの告発に対して自らを弁護するためにここへ来たわけではない。

ex.ja: 彼は無実の罪で告発されている。

note.ja: accuse（責める）+ -ation。ad（〜に）+ causa（訴訟・理由）。「訴えを起こすこと」→「非難・告発」。cause と同じ。

Determined by impulse rather than reason; often connoting heavy-handedness.

en: Any substance, especially food, used in catching fish, or other animals, by alluring them to a hook, snare, trap, or net.
Food containing poison or a harmful additive to kill animals that are pests.
To attract with bait; to entice.
To affix bait to a trap or a fishing hook or fishing line.
Obvious; blatant.
Well-known; famous; renowned.

ex.en: I put a bait on a hook.
ex.ja: 私は釣り針にえさを付けた。

ex.ja: 彼は釣り針に生き餌をつけた。

ex.en: I put bait on the hook.
ex.ja: 私は釣り針にえさを付けた。

en: To make a short, loud, explosive noise with the vocal organs (said of animals, especially dogs).
To make a clamor; to make importunate outcries.
The short, loud, explosive sound uttered by a dog, a fox, and some other animals.
An abrupt loud vocal utterance.
The sound of a dog barking.

bark.ety:
From Middle English barken, berken, borken, from Old English beorcan (“to bark”), from the Proto-West Germanic *berkan (“to bark”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰerg- (“to make a noise, growl, bark”), from *bʰer- (“to drone, hum, buzz”).
Cognate with Icelandic berkja (“to bark, bluster”), Icelandic barki (“throat, windpipe”), dialectal Lithuanian burgė́ti (“to growl, grumble, grouch, quarrel”), Serbo-Croatian brbljati (“to murmur”). For the noun, compare Old English beorc, bearce (“barking”).

ex.en: I heard a dog barking in the distance.
ex.ja: 犬が遠くで吠えているのが聞こえた。

ex.en: The dog next door kept barking all night.
ex.ja: 隣の家の犬が一晩中ほえ続けていたのです。

ex.en: The dog kept barking all through the night.
ex.ja: 犬は一晩中吠えどおしだった。

note.ja: 「ほえる」は古英語 beorcan（擬音的）から。「樹皮」は北欧語 börkr からで別語。

en: An item of clothing, usually underwear worn to support the breasts.

bra.ety: Clipping of brassiere, borrowed from French brassière, from Old French braciere (originally a lining inside armor to protect the arm, but later a garment), from Old French brace (“arm”), from Latin bracchia, plural of Latin bracchium (“forearm”), from Ancient Greek βραχίων (brakhíōn, “forearm”), from Proto-Hellenic *brəkʰús (“short”) (because the forearm is shorter than the upper arm), inherited from Proto-Indo-European *mréǵʰus.

ex.en: Yumiko has a push-up bra.
ex.ja: 優美子には谷間を強調するブラジャーがある。

ex.en: Please take off all your clothes except your underpants and bra.
ex.ja: パンツとブラジャー以外は全部脱いでください。

ex.en: Now that you mention it, she also needs a bra and panties.
ex.ja: 店員さんがそう言うなら、ブラジャーとパンティーも買ってってやろう。

note.ja: フランス語 brassière（胴着）の短縮。bras（腕）から。

en: The state of being brothers or a brother (also figuratively).
An association of people for any purpose, such as a society of monks; a fraternity.

brotherhood.ety: From Middle English brotherhod, equivalent to brother + -hood, from earlier brotherhede, alteration (influenced by suffixes in -hood, -head) of brotherrede (“brotherhood, fraternity”), from Old English brōþorrǣden (“brotherhood, fellowship”), equivalent to brother + -red (see brotherred). More at brother, -red. Piecewise doublet of friarhood.

ex.en: "Freedom, Equality, Brotherhood" is also Haiti's motto.
ex.ja: 「自由・平等・博愛」はハイチ共和国のスローガンでもある。

note.ja: brother（兄弟）+ -hood（状態・集団）。「兄弟の間柄」→「兄弟愛・団体」。

To make or become clear or easily understood; to explain or resolve in order to remove doubt or obscurity.

That which is compiled; especially, a book or document composed of materials gathering from other books or documents.

ex.ja: 草案を添付します。

ex.en: He devoted his whole life to compilation of the dictionary.
ex.ja: 彼は生涯を辞書の編さんに費やした。

To make up; to compose; to form.
